label: Mark 1:1
text: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

variants.reading: Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ('of Jesus Christ') - 'Son of God' absent
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' lists Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ('of Jesus Christ') in א* (Sinaiticus original hand) Θ 28 530 582* and others, against Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ υἱοῦ θεοῦ ('of Jesus Christ son of God') in B D L W (the NA text). Vaticanus includes 'Son of God'; only Sinaiticus's original hand omits it.

label: Mark 1:2
text:
As it is written in the prophets,
“Behold, I send my messenger before your face,
who will prepare your way before you:

variants.note: The fetched article lists ἐν τοῖς προφήταις ('in the prophets') in A E F G H K P W (Codex Washingtonianus) f13 and the Byzantine text - the Textus Receptus reading. The Alexandrian reading ἐν τῷ Ἠσαἲᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ ('in Isaiah the prophet') is carried by א (Sinaiticus) and B (Vaticanus).

label: Mark 1:3
text:
the voice of one crying in the wilderness,
‘Make ready the way of the Lord!
Make his paths straight!’”

label: Mark 1:4
text: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.

label: Mark 1:5
text: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.

label: Mark 1:6
text: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.

label: Mark 1:7
text: He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.

label: Mark 1:8
text: I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”

label: Mark 1:9
text: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

label: Mark 1:10
text: Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.

label: Mark 1:11
text: A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

label: Mark 1:12
text: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.

label: Mark 1:13
text: He was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.

label: Mark 1:14
text: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,

label: Mark 1:15
text:
and saying,
“The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”

label: Mark 1:16
text: Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

label: Mark 1:17
text:
Jesus said to them,
“Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”

label: Mark 1:18
text: Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.

label: Mark 1:19
text: Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.

label: Mark 1:20
text: Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.

label: Mark 1:21
text: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.

label: Mark 1:22
text: They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.

label: Mark 1:23
text: Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,

label: Mark 1:24
text: saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who you are: the Holy One of God!”

label: Mark 1:25
text:
Jesus rebuked him, saying,
“Be quiet, and come out of him!”

label: Mark 1:26
text: The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.

label: Mark 1:27
text: They were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”

label: Mark 1:28
text: The report of him went out immediately everywhere into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.

label: Mark 1:29
text: Immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

label: Mark 1:30
text: Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.

label: Mark 1:31
text: He came and took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.

label: Mark 1:32
text: At evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick, and those who were possessed by demons.

label: Mark 1:33
text: All the city was gathered together at the door.

label: Mark 1:34
text: He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.

label: Mark 1:35
text: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.

label: Mark 1:36
text: Simon and those who were with him followed after him;

label: Mark 1:37
text: and they found him, and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”

label: Mark 1:38
text:
He said to them,
“Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”

label: Mark 1:39
text: He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.

label: Mark 1:40
text: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”

label: Mark 1:41
text:
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him,
“I want to. Be made clean.”

variants.note: The fetched article lists ὀργισθεις ('irritated; angry') in D (Codex Bezae) ita ff2 r1, against σπλαγχνισθεις ('filled with compassion') in all other manuscripts. None of the D witnesses is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is left empty.

label: Mark 1:42
text: When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was made clean.

label: Mark 1:43
text: He strictly warned him, and immediately sent him out,

label: Mark 1:44
text:
and said to him,
“See you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”

label: Mark 1:45
text: But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places: and they came to him from everywhere.

statement: Mark attributed a combined quotation - Malachi 3:1 ('Behold, I send my messenger before your face') and Isaiah 40:3 ('the voice of one crying in the wilderness') - to Isaiah the prophet.
label: Mark 1:2-3 combined quotation under Isaiah's name

statement: John preached that one mightier than he was coming, whose sandal's thong he was not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
label: John unworthy to loosen the sandal's thong

statement: Jesus was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; he was with the wild animals, and angels served him.
label: Forty days tempted by Satan, with the wild animals

statement: On a Sabbath Jesus taught in the synagogue at Capernaum, and the congregation was astonished, for he taught as one having authority and not as the scribes.

statement: In the Capernaum synagogue Jesus rebuked an unclean spirit, and it came out of a man, amazing the congregation.

label: Capernaum (Mark-Luke synagogue story absent from Matthew)
title: Capernaum
excerpt: On a Sabbath day, Jesus taught in the synagogue in Capernaum and healed a man who was possessed by an unclean spirit ( Luke 4:31–36 and Mark 1:21–28 ). This story is notable as the only one that is common to the gospels of Mark and Luke but not contained in the Gospel of Matthew .
